payload.text:
GUARD-RAIL CONFLICT, surfaced not ruled (CLAUDE.md requires logging the conflict and handing it to the user; no work started).

The five stated threads, held against the record:

1. WATCHER — already shipped. chokidar in the engine, `sofar serve`, plus the doorbell SSE client and `sofar pull --watch` from sync-client 3.3. Nothing new required; any H2 work here is extension.

2. SYNC — already shipped, and explicitly blessed. sync-client is 15/15 tasks done: login by RFC-8628 device flow, link, push/pull with offline queue, ack cursors and doorbell SSE. SPEC Architectural invariants names it as the SOLE permitted egress: "The ONLY egress in the product is the v2 sync client (sync-client D4)". Note the CLAUDE.md rail "DO NOT build the sync service/backend" bites the SERVER, not the client — the client is done and sanctioned. Do not re-litigate it as forbidden.

3. SOFAR SHARES THE REQUIRED PIECE TO AGENTS — this is the product thesis, not a new capability, and it already has an implementation: core/index-tier1.ts is exactly "declared relevance, keyed for lookup" so the guard, the session-start priming line and mid-task search can each get only their piece. Extension work is unblocked.

4. MODEL ORCHESTRATION — already in flight as session-driver, and already cleared. session-driver D1 ruled that launching the operator's OWN agent process under the operator's own auth is not a model call, because that process's inference is the operator's and sofar needs no key, no call and no egress to launch it. Proceed there, not here.

5. FASTER INDEXING USING AI — THE ONLY GENUINE COLLISION, and it is blocked twice over, so it cannot be waved through:
   (a) SPEC Architectural invariants: "sofar never calls a model: no API keys, no inference costs, no user content fed to any model... Any change that would add a model call to sofar (e.g. cheap-model or Batch-API bookkeeping) is rejected until a Decision explicitly revisits this invariant (felt-cost D3)."
   (b) More pointedly, the indexing layer ALREADY faced this exact temptation and refused it. SPEC pins record-graph citation extraction as "a CLOSED LEXICAL GRAMMAR with literal matching only — no inference, no embeddings, no entity resolution", alongside a determinism law: the same records must build a deep-equal graph. Embedding-based indexing breaks determinism as well as the zero-model rule, so replay would stop being reproducible.

   A WAY THROUGH THAT COSTS NO RULING, worth considering before spending the invariant: apply the D1 carve-out one layer up. The operator's agent is already running and already paid for, so let IT produce the enrichment — summaries, groupings, relevance hints — and emit them as ordinary events in packages/schema that sofar only stores, folds and serves. sofar still never calls a model, holds no key, and sends nothing anywhere; determinism survives because the fold is still a pure function of the event set. What is lost is that enrichment becomes non-retroactive, produced only for records an agent has actually visited. If the user wants the OTHER version — sofar embedding records itself — that needs a Decision explicitly superseding both SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3, logged BEFORE any work, per the session-driver D1 amendment to the rails.

RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE, relevant because this session just settled it: the Rust/Zig verdict rested on sofar being IO-bound. Vector or embedding indexing is CPU-bound, and it is the one item on this roadmap that could flip that finding. If 5 lands in its embedding form, the runtime question reopens on merit and the artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ff9f4ee7-ede7-4d11-be78-d47eba7f206a must be revisited rather than cited.

payload.next_action: Rule on item 5, faster indexing using AI, before any work starts on it: either take the agent-emitted enrichment route, which needs no Decision because sofar still never calls a model, or log a Decision explicitly superseding SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3 for the embedding route, before the work and never after, per the guard-rail amendment in session-driver D1. Items 1 through 4 need nothing from this initiative and should be pursued in their own records.

payload.text:
CAVEAT on the "if it ever flips, rewrite the hook path in Rust" escape hatch this session has been recommending — it is less clean than stated, and the objection is already in the record.

speed-2 D1 chose the three-bundle split OVER, among others, "a second hand-written hook implementation (two sources of truth for hook behavior)", and its stated reason was that falling through on unrecognized argv shapes "keeps commander the single owner of the command surface, so --help, --version and every error message are byte-identical". A Rust hook binary is structurally the SAME rejected option: it would have to re-implement fast.ts's argv recognition and its fall-through to the full CLI, and the moment it recognizes a shape commander later changes, the two drift — which is exactly the divergence D1 refused.

So the escape hatch survives only under a condition that must be stated whenever it is offered: a native hook path has to either (a) own the entire command surface, which means porting commander's behaviour including help and error text byte-for-byte, or (b) accept the divergence risk D1 rejected, which needs a Decision naming D1. It is NOT the cheap few-hundred-line carve-out it looks like from the bundle split alone. The seam that makes the split cheap is a JS seam: dist/cli.js dynamically imports fast.js or full.js in the same runtime, and a native binary cannot fall through to full.js without paying the Node boot it was introduced to avoid — which is most of the win gone in exactly the cases it does not recognize.

Consequence for the verdict: the artifact at ff9f4ee7 and the typescript-7 decision both present "hook path only" as the graceful downgrade. That framing stands as a direction but understates its cost; if anyone acts on it, they must read speed-2 D1 first.

payload.next_action: Still item 5, faster indexing using AI, which is the only thing on this initiative that blocks work: choose the agent-emitted enrichment route, which needs no Decision, or log one superseding SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3 for the embedding route. If the Rust option is ever exercised, read speed-2 D1 first, per the escape-hatch caveat noted above.

The hook-path carve-out is therefore not the cheap few-hundred-line move it appears to be, and anyone acting on it must read speed-2 D1 first. Current Rust is 1.97 from July 2026 on edition 2024, with async closures, type alias impl Trait and the Polonius borrow checker as the notable recent additions; column header updated from the vague 1.0 since 2015. Verdict unchanged, and the reason is the point worth keeping: better Rust tooling lowers the cost of the port, it does not raise the benefit, which is still about 20ms of node boot on IO-bound work.

payload.text:
DEFINITION + honest limit of "agent-emitted enrichment", the route proposed for roadmap item 5.

THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS CODEBASE — it is not a new invention, it is a generalisation. sofar_log_decision already takes a `guard` argument: a machine-checkable glob list ("path:packages/schema/**", "cmd:*npm publish*") that the AGENT writes and sofar merely matches against later work. core/index-tier1.ts names the concept outright: "DECLARED relevance — does any decision ANYWHERE guard this path or command?" That is precisely the shape: the model supplies judgement, sofar supplies storage, matching and determinism. Item 5 would extend it — relevance links, topic tags, supersession edges, multi-granularity summaries — as new event types in packages/schema, emitted through tools the agent already calls.

WHY IT COSTS NO INVARIANT:
- sofar still never calls a model, holds no key and sends nothing off the machine. The inference is the operator's, already running, already paid for — the identical reasoning session-driver D1 used to legalise launching.
- The fold stays a pure function of the event set, so replay is still deterministic and the record-graph determinism law survives. Enrichment is just more events.
- Marginal inference cost is near zero: the agent already has the record in context, so emitting a tag is a few output tokens, not a new call. This SATISFIES felt-cost D3 rather than superseding it.

WHAT IT COSTS — state these whenever the route is offered:
1. Non-retroactive. Only records an agent actually visits get enriched; the existing 10,460 events stay bare unless something walks them, and walking them IS inference, merely the operator's.
2. Non-uniform. Different sessions and models tag differently. An embedding index is at least consistently wrong; this is inconsistently right.
3. Depends on agent compliance, which this repo already knows is imperfect — sessions skip sofar_start_session unless the Stop hook forces the issue.
4. THE REAL LIMIT, and the one that decides item 5: it yields DECLARED relevance, never DISCOVERED relevance. You cannot ask "find me records like this one" without embeddings. Agent-emitted enrichment buys a better index; it does not buy semantic search.

SO THE RULING IS A CHOICE OF GOAL, not of implementation. If the goal is a faster, richer index over things someone thought to connect, take this route and spend no invariant. If the goal is surfacing connections NOBODY declared, embeddings are the only answer and SPEC Architectural invariants plus felt-cost D3 must be explicitly superseded first. Do not adopt this route while intending the second goal — it will look like progress and then fail at exactly the query that motivated the feature.

payload.next_action: Rule item 5 by naming the GOAL first, not the implementation: if the goal is a faster and richer index over declared connections, take the agent-emitted enrichment route and no Decision is needed; if the goal is discovering connections nobody declared, log a Decision superseding SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3 before any work, since only embeddings answer that. Everything else on this initiative is already pointed at its own record.

payload.text:
ITEM 5, REVISED RECOMMENDATION: the two routes are not alternatives, they are LAYERS, and the earlier framing of "choose your goal" was too binary. Both are reachable, and doing them in the right order makes the expensive one cheaper and safer.

THE ARCHITECTURAL MOVE THAT MAKES BOTH POSSIBLE. The determinism law is only violated if inference runs INSIDE the fold. It is not violated if inference runs outside and its OUTPUT is recorded as ordinary events. The fold then stays exactly what it is — a pure function of the event set — and the non-determinism lives in a producer, outside, where it is tolerable and auditable. This is the same trick sofar's whole design already rests on: sofar never infers, it folds; let inference happen elsewhere and land as events.

So the shape is: enrichment event types live in packages/schema, and PRODUCERS are pluggable.
- Producer A, an agent mid-session: free, already paid for, no rule changed.
- Producer B, an explicit opt-in semantic pass: costs money, needs a Decision.
Both emit the SAME event types. Stamp the producer on each event so either can be dropped or recomputed without touching the other.

WHY THIS SHRINKS THE RULE CHANGE. If producer B is an opt-in, user-invoked command rather than a runtime dependency, the Decision needed is narrow: "an explicit opt-in command may call a model; the engine, hooks, MCP server and fold never do." A default install still makes zero model calls and the invariant holds for everyone who does not opt in. That is a far smaller hole than "sofar calls models", and it keeps the hot path and the no-key property intact — which is what SPEC Architectural invariants was actually protecting.

WHY WAY 2 MUST STILL GO FIRST — it is not a compromise, it is de-risking:
1. It defines the event types, the index and the query surface. Producer B then becomes just another writer into machinery already built and tested, instead of a new subsystem.
2. It produces LABELLED DATA. Declared relevance links are ground truth, so the question "are embeddings actually better than what agents already declare?" becomes measurable instead of assumed. Buying the expensive option before you can measure it is how you end up unable to tell whether it worked.
3. It costs nothing and blocks nothing, so there is no reason to sequence it second.

SEQUENCE: build Way 2 now with producer stamped on every enrichment event; run it long enough to have real declared links; then decide producer B against measured recall rather than intuition, with a narrowly scoped Decision. If discovery turns out to be the thing you actually needed, the only work left at that point is the producer itself.

Defer the semantic producer until there are real declared links to measure it against, then log a narrowly scoped Decision permitting a model call only from an explicit opt-in command, naming SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3.

payload.text:
Jev / System One audit (2026-09-19), for the "model orchestration" thread and its guard-rail conflict.

WHAT JEV IS. TypeSafe AI (Diogo Almeida, ex-OpenAI instruction-following; $40M seed led by DCVC; out of stealth 2026-09-15, early-access waitlist; also listed on Cloudflare Workers AI as typesafe/jev). A "System One model": POST /v1/systemone with {model:"jev-latest", state: string|object|array (text only, 32k tokens), questions: map of named typed questions}. Three primitives — Noul (P(yes) 0–1, no separate confidence), Choice (2–255 options → choice + probabilities + confidence), Score (2–10 ordered described levels → probability-weighted score + per-level probabilities + confidence). Questions in one request are evaluated INDEPENDENTLY and in parallel against the same state; no text generation, no tool args, no arithmetic, no date comparison, weak on negation/indirection. Trained with "RLCD" (RL for calibrated decisions); architecture undisclosed, no paper, no public calibration curve, vendor evals graded against the average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1. Pricing $0.042/M input, output free. Vendor claims 40–200x faster (70–500 ms end to end), up to 444x cheaper; batching 13 questions in one call measured 12.2x cheaper / 10x faster than 13 sequential calls.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE. paddo.dev: 9,081 product-match pairs, $0.32 total, 48/50 on hand review, bimodal probability shape, prompt injection via state text observed. Pydantic AI (issue #8472): extraction-by-selection 12/12; character spelling 0/8; tool-gate threshold 0.6 agreed with humans on 62/120 vs 43/120 at 0.8. HN (1.8k points): "can't hallucinate" is schema-only, confidently-wrong answers remain; one commenter rebuilt the shape with open encoder classifiers in ~2h — "the hard part is defining the answer distributions"; Doom demo fed coordinates not pixels. Ecosystem: LangChain ModelRouterMiddleware + AutoModeMiddleware (Sydney Runkle/Hunter Lovell, 2026-09-17 — the tweet only links that article); Pydantic AI TypeSafeModel; "instant compaction" (score each tool call for relevance, keep only relevant context).

RELATION TO THE INVARIANT. Jev IS a model call: API key, metered cost, record content leaves the machine. It defeats only the COST clause of §Architectural invariants / felt-cost D3 (a full 16k-token digest costs ~$0.0007 per judgement); the privacy clause (user content to a third party) and the dependency clause (key, network, waitlist, no paper) stand. Also 70–500 ms exceeds the 100 ms hook budget (speed T2), so it can never sit on a hook, statusline or shim path regardless of the ruling — only in the driver between sessions, in pull surfaces (sofar find / related / why), at write-back, and in offline passes (index, tune, bench loss study).

WHERE SOFAR DECIDES BY RULE TODAY (candidate judgement points): (1) driver handoff reason — stall = "no task status change" (drive.ts) → Noul "did this session advance task X?"; Score "how done is X?" as an acceptance gate; (2) route hints (routing.ts) hand-written per task → Choice over model×effort (LangChain's ModelRouter pattern); (3) "next action may be stale: N events since write-back" is a count → Noul per event "does this invalidate the next action?"; (4) digest budget (token-optimization, digest-signal) → Score relevance of each decision/note/adjacent initiative to the next task, inject only what scores; (5) record graph is "adjacency, not aboutness" → Noul "does initiative A bear on task B?" turns it into aboutness for find/related/why (C8); (6) rejected approaches / cross-initiative-conflicts → Noul at log_decision time "does this proposal re-propose R?" (C3); (7) tune/suggest never labels a cause by design — leave alone; (8) citations are a closed lexical grammar by contract — leave alone.

HONEST MULTIPLIERS. Agent billed tokens (C1): injection is ~1k of a ~200k session, so relevance-filtered injection moves C1 by ~1%, not 10x. Unattended driving (C4) and re-violation (C3) and why-accuracy (C8) are where a judge could plausibly give 2–5x on the specific failure modes (wasted stall sessions, re-proposed rejected approaches, adjacency false positives), but nothing is measured; bench-refresh is the instrument and a "sofar + judge" arm would be the test. No 10x claim is supportable today.

WHAT CAN BE BUILT WITHOUT VIOLATING THE INVARIANT NOW. The durable, provider-independent work is Jev's SHAPE, not its model: a Judge seam in the engine — typed questions (noul/choice/score) over record state, answers carrying probabilities, confidence-gated escalation (high → act, mid → ask via needs_user, low → refuse) — with a DETERMINISTIC default implementation (today's counts and lexical rules re-expressed as answers with confidence 1.0 or 0.5) and a provider slot an operator may fill by explicit opt-in. Answer spaces (the questions above) are the hard part per HN and cost nothing to define. Only the provider slot needs the narrowly scoped Decision the roadmap-h2 next action already anticipates (naming §Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3), logged before any provider code.

RISKS TO CARRY INTO THE RULING: early access only; 32k state (digest fits, events.jsonl does not); prompt injection through record text an agent wrote; no calibration evidence, so thresholds must be validated on our own ground truth (bench-refresh hidden tests); text-only and date-blind, so staleness arithmetic stays in code.
